svg.title: Japan Infographic
svg.desc: An editorial infographic about Japan covering geography, GDP trends, population demographics, and travel destinations.

div.style: font-family:'Noto Sans JP', sans-serif; color: #444; line-height: 1.8; font-size: 18px;
div.p: Japan is an archipelago of over 6,800 islands located off the eastern coast of Asia. Known for its ancient traditions merging seamlessly with cutting-edge technology, it is a land of contrasts featuring neon-lit metropolises, serene mountain retreats, and historic temples.

With a rich cultural heritage spanning thousands of years, Japan has influenced global fashion, art, cuisine, and pop culture. From the iconic cherry blossoms of spring to the powder snow of Hokkaido, every season brings a unique experience to this resilient nation.
The country operates under a constitutional monarchy with the Emperor serving as the symbolic head of state, while modern democratic processes drive policy and innovation.

div.style: display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; height:100%; font-family:'Noto Sans JP', sans-serif; color:#666; font-style:italic;

foreignObject.div: "In Japan, tradition is not something you remember, but something you do." — Yukio Mishima

g.text: Japan has the world's 4th largest economy by nominal GDP. While it held steady for several years, recent fluctuations reflect global currency shifts and inflation impacts. Data represents Nominal GDP in Current US$ Trillions.

foreignObject.div: Neon lights, Shibuya Crossing, Senso-ji Temple, Imperial Palace.
Kinkaku-ji, Fushimi Inari Shrine, Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, Geisha District.
Dotonbori street food, Osaka Castle, Universal Studios Japan, Aquarium.
Peace Memorial Park, Itsukushima Shrine floating gate.
Views of Mt. Fuji, Lake Kawaguchi, Hot springs (Onsen).
Niseko Skiing, Sapporo Snow Festival, Lavender fields, Seafood markets.

g.text: Sources: World Bank (GDP data 2015-2023 estimates), Statistics Bureau of Japan (2023 Census). Map not to scale.
